item.title: Modeling Asymmetries in Be Star Disks Using Spectro-interferometric H-alpha Observations from the CHARA Array's VEGA Instrument
item.description: arXiv:2611.26728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Be stars are rapidly rotating B-type stars with outflowing decretion disks. The observational record shows that in many cases the peaks of their H$\alpha$ flux profile vary on long timescales. These changes are probably caused by the development of disk brightness asymmetries that are related to global disk oscillation modes. Here we present spectro-interferometric observations made with the CHARA Array interferometer and the VEGA beam combiner that document the interferometric data across the H$\alpha$ line for the Be stars $\gamma$ Cas, $\phi$ Per, $\zeta$ Tau, and $\beta$ CMi. The differential interferometric visibility amplitudes and phases across the H$\alpha$ emission line reveal clues about the asymmetries present in their disks. Here we describe a model of the H$\alpha$ formation that calculates the emission intensity at spatial positions around the star and disk. The parameters describing the disk and the oscillation mode are optimized to match the interferometric data and contemporaneous H$\alpha$ spectroscopy. The analysis confirms the presence of strong disk asymmetries at the time of the observations (2020) in the cases of $\gamma$ Cas and $\phi$ Per, and hints that weaker oscillation modes were also present in the disks of $\zeta$ Tau and $\beta$ CMi. The success of this single epoch study demonstrates the promise of future interferometric programs to investigate how the modes precess within the disk and grow and decline over time.
item.dc:creator: Peter Wysocki, Douglas Gies, Denis Mourard, Atsuo Okazaki, Fabien Baron, Gail Schaefer

item.title: Magnetic vector potentials and helicity in periodic domains
item.description: arXiv:2611.26901v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a magnetic field in three-dimensional Euclidean space, we argue about the existence of a magnetic vector potential in a finite cuboid with periodic boundary conditions. We first argue in physical terms by representing periodic domains as tori and show that in some cases, the generating electric current is unphysical. We then represent magnetic fields and vector potentials as differential 2 and 1-forms. For a given magnetic field we ask the question whether a corresponding vector potential exists. Singly periodic domains are shown to always allow for a vector potential. For doubly periodic domains it only exists if the net magnetic flux through the non-periodic dimension vanishes, while for triply periodic domains the net flux must vanish in all directions. This has implications for the definition of magnetic helicity in periodic domains. We show that periodic domains together with a mean magnetic flux lead to contradicting results about the value of the magnetic helicity and we show in a few thought experiments fundamental contradictions to the interpretation as the linking of magnetic field lines. For the helicity we can even construct magnetic fields in periodic domains for which the magnetic helicity exists, but the calculations of the magnetic helicity do not lead to meaningful results due to the gauge freedom. With that we conclude that in presence of a mean magnetic field the calculated magnetic helicity cannot be interpreted geometrically in a straightforward way. However, using the winding gauge we can recover the geometric interpretation of the helicity as the flux averaged magnetic field line winding. Finally, for the solar relevant non-periodic domain with finite point-wise flux and zero integrated flux, using an appropriate gauge transformation the magnetic helicity can be shown to vanish. The winding helicity, however, would lead to a non-vanishing value here.
item.dc:creator: Simon Candelaresi

item.title: Accretor Luminosity as Probe of Orbital Evolution and Magnetic Braking in AM CVn Binaries
item.description: arXiv:2611.26973v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: AM CVn binaries are ultracompact systems with orbital periods $P_{\rm orb} \lesssim 70$ min, where a white dwarf accretes from a He-rich semidegenerate donor. At short orbital periods ($P_{\rm orb} \lesssim 20$ min), rapid accretion reheats the accretor. As the system widens and the mass transfer rate decreases, the accretor follows standard white dwarf cooling at longer orbital periods ($P_{\rm orb} \gtrsim 30$ min). The accretor cooling luminosity then acts as a powerful probe into the orbital evolution of the binary. Recent observations show that the accretor appears brighter (younger) at long orbital periods, compared to models where orbital angular momentum loss is solely set by gravitational wave emission. We show that additional angular momentum loss, which we ascribe to magnetic braking of the donor, can better reproduce observations of accretor luminosity. We test and constrain various proposed magnetic braking formalisms, for the white dwarf, helium star, and evolved cataclysmic variable (CV) channels for AM CVn formation. None of the magnetic braking formalisms in their original form can reproduce the observations, but the widely popular magnetic braking proposed by Rappaport et al. 1983 boosted by a factor $\approx 5$, or the saturated magnetic braking proposed by Matt et al. 2015 boosted by a factor of $\approx 150$, yields satisfactory results. We also find that the CARB formalism, recently applied to the evolved CV channel, is strongly in tension with observations of accretor luminosity. Our models motivate UV spectroscopy observations, and dedicated WD atmosphere models for AM CVn accretors.
item.dc:creator: Tin Long Sunny Wong, Peter Scherbak, Jim Fuller

item.title: Precise Radii of Visual Binaries with Dynamical Masses: $\xi$ Bootis $\&$ 70 Ophiuchi
item.description: arXiv:2611.27031v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A new orbital solution for $\xi$ Bootis (GJ 566 AB, P=152 yrs) and the recently revised orbital solution for 70 Ophiuchi (GJ 702 AB, P=88 yrs) yield component masses precise to 0.4\%. Their relatively wide separations ($>0.4^{\prime\prime}$) allow the components to be studied independently, making them ideal for testing the predictions of stellar evolutionary models. We use the six-telescope near-infrared MIRC-X and MYSTIC beam combiners at the CHARA Array to measure the angular diameters of all 4 stars. Combined with precise Gaia DR3 parallax values and bolometric fluxes, these interferometric measurements translate to stellar radii that are precise to $<2.4\%$ and effective temperatures precise to $<1.7\%$. We compare the measured radii and temperatures to four stellar evolutionary models (Lyon, Dartmouth, PARSEC, MIST). Over the mass range $0.67 - 0.91$ M$_\odot$, all models reproduce the observed properties within a few standard deviations, with no systematic offsets. The pairs are coeval and consistent with independent age estimates, further validating model predictions. With physical separations greater than 20 au, these pairs show no evidence of radius inflation, despite being spectroscopically classified as chromospherically active, and in the case of $\xi$ Bootis, probable members of the adolescent age ($\sim 0.4$ Gyr) Ursa Majoris Moving Group. In contrast, a set of 21 short-period ($P\lesssim$ 10 days) eclipsing binary stars with similar dynamical masses and metallicities are larger and often cooler than these same model predictions. Within this mass range, radius inflation appears to be associated with short-period binary star systems.

item.title: Ultraviolet Observations of Solar Active Phenomena
item.description: arXiv:2611.27071v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Ultraviolet observations of the Sun have revolutionized our understanding of the structure and dynamics of the solar atmosphere. From the chromosphere all the way to the corona, there are ubiquitous jets due to magnetic reconnection and associated with type III radio bursts. Sporadic flares occur in the corona, representing an inevitable breakup of magnetic energy accumulation as new magnetic flux continues to pump into the solar atmosphere, which is further shuffled by solar surface motions. Once large-scale eruptions occur, magnetized plasmas are expelled out into the interplanetary space, leaving globally propagating waves and the following dimmings. The waves can be utilized to diagnose the coronal magnetic field which cannot be measured directly, and the dimmings can be used to estimate the ejected mass of eruptions and magnetic connectivity. Extreme ultraviolet spectroscopic observations provide information on the fractionation of different chemical elements, in particular those elements with low first ionization potential. Thanks to the high spatial resolution of solar observations, all these results are believed to shed light on our understanding of the activity on other stars which cannot be imaged.
item.dc:creator: P. F. Chen, G. Del Zanna, L. Feng, J. H. Guo, Y. J. Hou, H. Tian, D. Tripathi

item.title: Interstellar extinction estimates for nearly 90 million stars based on synthetic photometry from Gaia XP spectra
item.description: arXiv:2611.27303v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Accurate stellar extinction measurements are essential for recovering intrinsic stellar properties and investigating the three-dimensional distribution of interstellar dust. We present reddening estimates for 87,270,425 stars using synthetic SMSS gri photometry derived from corrected Gaia DR3 XP spectra, combined with Gaia BP and RP, 2MASS JHKs, and WISE W1 photometry. Stellar extinction is determined through empirical SED fitting based on reference stellar loci constructed separately for dwarfs and giants. Comparisons with three external extinction catalogs show good overall agreement, with dispersions of 0.049-0.075 mag in E(B-V). The catalog covers approximately 99.99% of the sky. Using stars with sigma_d/d < 0.2, we further construct reddening maps in four distance ranges from 0 to 5 kpc, revealing prominent molecular clouds and large-scale Galactic dust structures. Extinction-corrected color-absolute-magnitude diagrams show significantly tighter stellar sequences and consistent red-clump features in different Galactic fields. The resulting catalog provides a homogeneous data set for stellar extinction correction and studies of Galactic dust structure.
item.dc:creator: Bao-Kun Sun, Yan-Hui Chen, Zheng Yu, Bai-Song Zhang

item.title: Characterising stellar photometry with invertible neural networks: Joint inference of stellar parameters and extinction
item.description: arXiv:2611.27342v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We introduce an extension to a simulation-based deep-learning approach for the characterisation of stellar photometry and investigate the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar properties and extinction. We used the PARSEC stellar evolutionary models to train a conditional invertible neural network (cINN) to jointly estimate full posterior distributions of stellar parameters and extinction. We tested our cINN on synthetic data and real Gaia+2MASS photometry of the two star-forming regions Taurus and Upper Scorpius. We compared our predicted extinction maps to two independent catalogues based on Gaia XP-spectra. On synthetic test data, our trained cINN exhibited a good predictive performance, achieving root mean squared errors (RMSEs) for the maximum a posteriori point estimates of about 0.16 mag for $A_V$, 0.07 dex for $\log(T_{eff}/K)$, 0.16 dex for $\log(g/cms^{-2})$, 0.2 dex for $\log(L/L\odot)$ and 0.1 dex for $\log(M_{ini}/M_\odot)$. Only $\log(age/yr)$ has proven harder to constrain with an RMSE of 0.56 dex. On the Gaia+2MASS observations of Taurus and Upper Scorpius, we retrieved reasonable extinction maps, exhibiting structures that are visually consistent with local clouds. Compared to the independent XP-spectra-based extinction studies, we found a good qualitative agreement and recovered the same prominent spatial structures. Quantitatively, however, we identified an average systematic overestimation of extinction in our approach of 0.5-0.7 mag compared to the spectroscopic studies. We investigated these offsets and identified photometric and distance uncertainties, which are currently unaccounted for in our approach, as likely causes. In conclusion, we demonstrated the feasibility of jointly estimating stellar parameters and extinction with our cINN approach, making it a promising avenue to further pursue for robust and efficient analysis of large photometric surveys.
item.dc:creator: Victor F. Ksoll, Isabelle Joncour, Prasanta Gorai, Ralf S. Klessen

item.title: Characterisation of B-type stars in four young Galactic open clusters. II. Photometric variability with TESS and identification of pulsating stars
item.description: arXiv:2611.27680v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Pulsations and binarity are important properties of massive stars and influence their structure and evolution. Young open clusters are ideal laboratories to study massive stars, since they are mostly coeval and chemically homogeneous. We analyse 82 B-type stars in the Galactic open clusters $h$ and $\chi$ Persei, NGC 457, NGC 581, and NGC 1960, which have ages between 15 and 30 Myr. We extract light curves using both simple aperture photometry and a point-spread-function-based method that minimises contamination from crowded fields in full-frame images from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission. We successfully extract light curves for 63 stars. The majority have photometric variability caused by pulsations, showing how pulsations are a common property of young B-type stars in clusters. We classify stars into different pulsator types based on their spectral type and frequency spectrum. The most common pulsator class are beta Cephei stars, with 29 stars in total, and we discover pulsation modes in almost all stars with a spectral type of B2 or earlier. All Be stars show pulsations, which supports the consensus of the ubiquity of pulsations in these stars. Finally, we confirm that the majority of early B-type stars are in binary systems, except for two pulsating Be stars and a star with rotational modulation. This indicates that pulsations do not significantly bias the spectroscopic detection of short-period binaries, except for Be stars where the spectroscopic radial velocity variability threshold should be higher than the typical value of 20 km s$^{-1}$.
item.dc:creator: Federica Nardini, Dominic M. Bowman, Julia Bodensteiner, Pieterjan Van Daele, Laura J. A. Scott, Keegan Thomson-Paressant, Jan Henneco, Hugues Sana

item.title: Atmospheric parameters and chemical abundances of young stars with APOGEE -- II. Carbon, Nitrogen, Oxygen, and Sulphur abundances in Orion
item.description: arXiv:2611.27952v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We derived the abundances of carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, sulphur, and iron in young G-, K-, and M-type stars (effective temperatures of 3500--5900 K) using APOGEE-2 infrared spectra. Our final sample comprises 195 slow rotators ($v\sin i$ $\leq$ 30 km~s$^{-1}$) in the Orion complex (Orion A, B, OB1, and $\lambda$~Ori). The abundances were determined using MARCS model atmospheres, atmospheric parameters derived with \tona, and the \bacc\ code. We obtained median abundances of $\epsilon$(C) = 8.37$\pm$0.10, $\epsilon$(N) = 7.35$\pm$0.16, $\epsilon$(O) = 8.63$\pm$0.08, $\epsilon$(S) = 7.19$\pm$0.18, and $\epsilon$(Fe) = 7.45$\pm$0.05. Nitrogen is subsolar ([N/H] $=-0.48$), whereas carbon, oxygen, sulphur, and iron are within 0.1 dex of the solar values. We find no spatial structure within the Orion subgroups, and the only significant difference is a 0.29 dex lower nitrogen abundance in Orion A than in Orion OB1, which does not extend to the other elements. Compared with 430 nearby main-sequence stars analysed in the same way, Orion shows carbon, nitrogen, and oxygen abundances lower by 0.1--0.2 dex, although consistent within the errors, whereas sulphur and iron differ by less than 0.07 dex. We also compare our abundances with nebular abundances of HII regions and star-forming galaxies: the stellar abundances of oxygen, sulphur, and iron are higher, with the largest offset in iron, although the agreement in abundance ratios improves when temperature inhomogeneities and dust depletion are taken into account.
item.dc:creator: Ricardo L\'opez-Valdivia, A. Z. Lugo-Aranda, Sergio S\'anchez-Sanju\'an, J. E. M\'endez-Delgado, Carlos G. item.title: Recovering buoyancy-glitch parameters in low-luminosity red giants from global stellar properties with machine learning
item.description: arXiv:2611.27954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Buoyancy glitches in red giants provide localized information on the interior structure near the base of the convective envelope, but their properties are typically inferred from dedicated seismic modelling rather than global properties, limiting large-sample applications. We investigate whether the buoyancy-glitch amplitude ($A_g$), location ($W_{\rm g}^{\star}$), and width ($D_g$) can be recovered from global stellar properties using gradient-boosted tree regressors (XGBoost and LightGBM). The models were trained on a grid of 12580 synthetic stellar models of low-luminosity red giants, with target parameters derived from fits to the local buoyancy frequency profile. We find that $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ exhibit excellent recoverability, achieving test-set $\mathcal{R}^2$ values of 0.98 and 0.97, respectively. In contrast, $A_g$ shows moderate recoverability overall ($\mathcal{R}^2=0.68$). This reduced recoverability of $A_g$ is concentrated in the large frequency separation range $\Delta\nu = 4.6$--$18.9\,\mu$Hz, where the glitch resides in the evanescent-zone transition between the convective envelope and the gravity-mode cavity, increasing intrinsic scatter. SHAP analysis shows that $\nu_{\rm max}$ and $T_{\rm eff}$ dominate the predictions across all targets, indicating that the regressors rely primarily on evolutionary state. While $W_{\rm g}^{\star}$ and $D_g$ are tightly constrained by global evolutionary trends, the lower recoverability of $A_g$ reflects localized structural complexity associated with red-giant evolution. Overall, for the synthetic grid adopted here, these results indicate that global properties provide a direct estimate of the buoyancy-glitch parameters and a way to prioritise dedicated mixed-mode inversions for large asteroseismic samples such as Kepler and PLATO.
item.dc:creator: Jiang Chen

item.title: Stellar activity demotes GJ 9404 b to a planetary candidate
item.description: arXiv:2611.26667v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: GJ 9404 is a nearby M dwarf ($d=23.8\,\text{pc}$), around which a $13.4586^{+0.0044}_{-0.0067}\,\text{d}$ planet has been claimed in a recent study using 54 publicly available HARPS-N radial velocities (RVs). We re-analyse the spectroscopy associated with this study, and carry out a joint modelling of: (i) stellar rotation in RV, FWHM, and Mount Wilson S-index through Gaussian processes; (ii) long-term trends in all physical quantities; (iii) planetary signals in RV. Current evidence supports the existence of planets in the period range $2-100\,\text{d}$ by at most $\Delta\ln Z=-0.4$ for any considered stellar-activity model, which is insufficient for a widely accepted planet detection. Additional spectroscopy is necessary to accurately quantify the stellar activity of GJ 9404 and determine whether any RV signals warrant further attention.
item.dc:creator: Atanas K. Stefanov, Alejandro Su\'arez Mascare\~no, Jonay I. Gonz\'alez Hern\'andez, Paul Charpentier, Nicola Nari, Rafael Rebolo, Thomas A. Baycroft

item.title: Machine learning reveals new Galactic C-rich and O-rich AGB sources
item.description: arXiv:2611.26701v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Identification of carbon-rich (C-rich) and oxygen-rich (O-rich) Asymptotic Giant Branch (AGB) stars is crucial to understanding the structure and dust sources of the Milky Way. We present a machine-learning (ML) classification of Galactic AGB candidates using Gaia DR3, identifying 304,090 O-rich and 4,227 C-rich sources. Our two-step approach, which involves similarity-based selection, followed by XGBoost classification that combines colour and spectroscopic features, demonstrates that a small, but high-quality training sample is sufficient for accurate identification even in massive datasets such as ~140 million sources from Gaia DR3. The ML-identified stars occupy distinct regions in colour-magnitude and Gaia-2MASS diagrams, and comparison with stellar isochrones combined with Gaia distances allows estimates of their masses and ages. Spatial distributions show that O-rich AGB stars dominate the inner Galaxy, while C-rich AGB stars are concentrated toward the anti-Galactic centre. Vertical profiles indicate that massive O-rich (5-8 M$_\odot$) stars remain near the Galactic mid-plane, whereas C-rich (2.3-2.5 M$_\odot$) and low-mass O-rich (1-1.5 M$_\odot$) AGB stars are more vertically extended, with scale heights that increase with decreasing stellar mass and increasing stellar ages. C-rich AGB stars trace the Galactic warp at intermediate ages (1 Gyr), with warp amplitudes appearing larger than those traced by Cepheids. Intermediate-mass O-rich AGB stars (~300 Myr) show tentative correspondence with several spiral arm features, while the C-rich distribution is too smooth for reliable identification with the current sample. These results highlight AGB stars as powerful probes of stellar evolution and Galactic dynamical processes.
item.dc:creator: Tanya Kushwahaa, Mikako Matsuura, Jason A. S. Hunt, Daisuke Kawata, Roger Wesson, Timothy A. Davis

item.title: Searching for substellar companion candidates with Gaia IV. New planetary-mass companions found in debris disks
item.description: arXiv:2611.26774v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: When spatially resolved, debris disks often exhibit structures (gaps, rings, and spirals) that may indicate the presence of unseen planetary-mass companions. However, such planets have not been detected in most cases. Gaia opens a new mass-separation parameter space for detecting unseen planets. A tool named GaiaPMEX has been developed to detect and characterize companions to stars. It is based on two binarity indicators derived from DR3: the Gaia astrometric signature and, when the sources were also observed by Hipparcos, the Gaia-Hipparcos proper motion anomaly. We used GaiaPMEX on 94 stars hosting resolved debris disks to search for companions. When companions were identified, we combined GaiaPMEX results with high-contrast imaging and radial velocity data to further constrain their mass and orbital properties. We found stellar or substellar companions around five targets (HD 54341, HD 146897, HD 206893, HD 107146, and HD 106906) and indications (2 sigma) for companions around three additional targets (BD+45 598, TWA 7, and HD 120326). The companion to the 150 Myr star HD 107146, which harbors a ring-like dust disk, is found to be a 2-6 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting between 2-10 au. A massive 3-20 Jupiter-mass companion is found 3-10 au from the close binary HD 106906, which already hosts a remote planet orbiting at more than 700 au, and an edge-on disk. The tentative companions to TWA 7 and HD 120326 are planetary-mass companions at 1-3 au. Both stars host a multiple-ring system. We finally provide meaningful upper limits on the possible presence of companions in the range of 0-100 au around a few emblematic stars (49 Cet, AU Mic, beta Pic, and epsilon Eri) and stars hosting well-defined ring-like structures.
item.dc:creator: A. -M. Lagrange, S. Toucheboeuf, F. Kiefer, P. Rubini, J. Milli, L. Matr., H. Beust, C. Perrot, M. M. lin, A. Boccaletti, C. Wilkinson, P. Delorme

item.title: The Effect of Dust Grain Growth and Stellar Metallicity on Gas Giant Planet Formation by Disk Instability
item.description: arXiv:2611.26804v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The formation of gas giant planets by the gas disk gravitational instability (GDGI) mechanism depends sensitively on the thermodynamics of the protoplanetary disk gas: disk gas must be able to cool on orbital timescales for dense clumps to become gravitationally unstable and contract to form protoplanets. Since disk cooling is regulated by the opacity of the dust grains embedded in the gas, the properties of these dust grains are critical for the GDGI mechanism. Grain growth to larger sizes than assumed in traditional opacity models for solar metallicity, as well as protostars with sub-solar metallicity, should have lower opacity disks that are more conducive to planet formation by GDGI. Here we use a three dimensional radiative hydrodynamics and gravitation code to compute the evolution of the GDGI in $0.091 M_\odot$ disks with varied initial minimum values (1.3 to 2.7) of the Toomre criterion orbiting solar-mass protostars. Three sets of eight models are computed: one with the standard opacity, and two more with the opacity reduced by arbitrary factors of 10 or 100. As expected, the reduced opacity models result in enhanced disk fragmentation by the GDGI and the production of more self-gravitating clumps than the standard opacity models. Nevertheless, all three opacities form similar self-gravitating clumps at this early phase of clump evolution, with masses of 0.2 to 0.7 $M_{Jup}$ and semimajor axes between 6 and 13 au. Significant dust grain growth should enhance the ability of the GDGI to form protoplanets around super-solar metallicity protostars.
item.dc:creator: Alan P. Boss

item.title: Determining the Spin and Orbital Period of the Asynchronous Cataclysmic Variable X10 in 47 Tucanae
item.description: arXiv:2611.26880v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The X-ray source X10 in the globular cluster 47 Tuc has been identified as a cataclysmic variable (CV). With a suggested 4.7 hour periodicity, and a soft X-ray spectrum, it appears to be an unusually X-ray luminous ($L_X=2.2\times10^{32}$ erg s$^{-1}$) polar CV. We use 286 ks of Chandra X-ray Observatory observations of 47 Tuc to study the X-ray timing behavior of 47 Tuc X10. X10 shows clear pulsations in the data, with occasional phase shifts. These suggest that X10 is an asynchronous polar CV, where the spin and orbital periods are slightly misaligned, and the dominant accretion flow shifts from one pole to the other. We use a Lomb-Scargle periodogram to suggest potential spin and orbital periods, then model the X-ray lightcurve using simple sinusoids to represent emission from each accretion pole, switching which pole is visible on the beat period. We find a white dwarf spin period of $P_{\mathrm{spin}} = 4.2683$ h and derive an orbital period of $P_{\mathrm{orb}} = 4.6779$ h from the beat modulation. This large degree of asynchronism (8.8%) suggests that X10 is in an unstable equilibrium, and may be a transitional system between an intermediate polar and a fully synchronized polar.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Mendoza-Fredes, Craig O. Heinke, Matthew Lang, Asma Hattawi

item.title: Hard X-ray spectroscopy of a short-period asynchronous polar: IGR J19552+0044
item.description: arXiv:2611.27508v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: IGR J19552+0044 is an asynchronous polar with a beat modulation of $\approx2$ days due to $\approx3$% spin-orbit asynchronism. We present the first hard X-ray properties of this system using a NuSTAR observation. Spectral modeling yields a shock temperature of $kT_{\rm s}=44.50^{+3.60}_{-3.29}$ keV, implying a white dwarf mass of $M_{\rm WD}\geq 0.85\,M_\odot$. We infer an average accretion rate of $\dot{M}\sim 3.0\times 10^{-11}\,M_\odot\,{\rm yr}^{-1}$, consistent with expectations for short-period systems (orbital period $<2$ h). Even at this low accretion rate, we detect a significant Compton reflection component that gives a shock height of $H\sim 0.3\,R_{\rm WD}$. Time-resolved spectroscopy of the observation, covering $\approx61$% of a beat cycle, reveals a variation in $\dot{M}$ by a factor of $\sim 4.5$, providing X-ray evidence for the magnetic valve mechanism. Despite the large variations in $\dot{M}$, no significant change in shock temperature is observed. This weak thermal response constrains the shock structure on the white dwarf surface, favoring a shock height that remains approximately constant as $\dot{M}$ changes, potentially due to variations in the fractional accretion area $f$.
item.dc:creator: Akash Agarwal, Vikram Rana

item.title: Nuclear Precision and Multimessenger Constraints on Neutron-Star Structure
item.description: arXiv:2611.27669v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Neutron-star cores retain structural freedom beyond the constraints supplied by nuclear measurements. We quantify this freedom through an observable-dependent variance ceiling and identify radius--Love compensation as a mechanism suppressing nuclear constraints on tides. Across four data-conditioned equation-of-state families, a pulsar radius measured to 0.3 km paired with a binary tide measured to 10\% removes 44--68\% of the current logarithmic Love-number variance. The framework connects laboratory precision and complementary stellar measurements to core structure.
item.dc:creator: Hisham Anwer, A. Adel, E. Omar

item.title: PHOTO-CAT - Photometric Contamination Analyzer Tool: A High-Performance Framework for Photometric Contamination Assessment
item.description: arXiv:2611.27677v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: High-precision photometric missions are sensitive to flux contamination from neighboring stars, which can bias light curves, dilute transit depths, and compromise photometric precision. We present PHOTO-CAT, a catalog-driven, mission-agnostic tool for quantifying stellar flux contamination in photometric observations. The tool builds a three-dimensional Euclidean representation of the sky from a user-provided astrometric catalog, indexes it with a memory-optimized KDTree for rapid neighbor searches, and computes per-target contamination metrics from angular separation, relative fluxes, and configurable aperture models (top-hat or circular Gaussian PSF), optionally converted into an arbitrary instrumental bandpass via empirical photometric relations or stellar spectral models. A streaming, CSR-style storage format with compact internal identifiers enables scalable processing of catalogs with tens to hundreds of millions of sources with minimal memory overhead. Outputs include per-target contaminating flux, contamination ratios, target purity, number of neighboring sources, and their angular separations, supporting target screening and field-selection decisions ahead of observations. We demonstrate the software performance on all-sky Gaia samples (G <= 12, with neighbors down to G = 17; over three million targets), providing global contamination statistics and spatial characterization of crowded regions, and apply it to the Ariel Mission Candidate Sample to show how wavelength-dependent contamination estimates support target selection and observing-geometry optimization. Although developed for the Mauve satellite, PHOTO-CAT is mission-agnostic and readily applicable to TESS, PLATO, Ariel, and other surveys.
item.dc:creator: G. Galletta, F. Favata, L. Bradley, A. Saba, R. Grant, J. McLaren, S. Harvey, M. Tessenyi, G. Micela

item.title: Precise Interstellar Extinction Estimates for Nearly Ten Million Stars Based on Multiple Spectroscopic Surveys
item.description: arXiv:2611.27773v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Accurate interstellar extinction estimates are vital for revealing the intrinsic physical properties of stars and the dynamic structure of the Milky Way. Based on multiple optical and near-infrared spectroscopic surveys, including LAMOST, APOGEE, GALAH, GaiaESO, SEGUE, and DESI, we use MLPs and polynomial regressions to calibrate giants and dwarfs separately onto the APOGEE parameter scale, constructing a combined spectroscopic catalog of nearly ten million stars with calibrated stellar atmospheric parameters. This catalog not only provides a robust dataset for our extinction measurements, but also serves as a reference sample for estimating stellar parameters from photometric surveys. Both cross-survey comparisons and external comparisons with high-resolution spectroscopic benchmarks show good agreement in the calibrated parameters. By applying the star-pair method to this extensive sample, we obtain precise extinction estimates. Incorporating distance information, we characterize the spatial distribution of extinction covering over 33,000 square degrees of the sky. Comparisons with existing literature demonstrate that our extinction estimates achieve an exceptional precision of 0.019-0.022 mag. The value-added catalog and open-source Python pipeline for line-of-sight extinction released in this work will provide robust support for future Galactic structure studies and photometric calibrations.

item.title: Millimeter-wave Detections of Symbiotic Stars in SPT and ACT Data
item.description: arXiv:2605.01022v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present the results of a joint targeted search of candidate symbiotic stars at millimeter wavelengths using the South Pole Telescope (SPT) and the Atacama Cosmology Telescope (ACT). Candidates are selected from the New Online Database of Symbiotic Variables, restricting to objects that are within either the SPT-3G or ACT~DR6 footprint, covering most of the southern hemisphere and up to a declination of $+20^\circ$. Forced photometry on the 828 candidate symbiotic star locations in SPT and ACT data results in 31 unique objects detected with more than a $3\sigma$ significance using two frequency bands: 18 confirmed and 13 suspected symbiotic stars. We provide the SPT and ACT 95/98, 150, and 220~GHz light curves, along with optical and infrared light curves from 2016--2026, as well as spectral energy distributions, physical parameters from the literature, and brief summaries regarding the nature of each individual object. Using Herschel SPIRE data from 2013, we place upper limits on millimeter flux for CN Cha near the beginning of the optical rise in its 2012/2013 nova, which suggests a strong variability and lag at millimeter wavelengths and results in a rare observance of a Galactic millimeter slow transient. In addition, we provide coadded thumbnails and light curves for the remaining 797 candidate symbiotic stars that did not pass our detection thresholds. Millimeter-wave emission from symbiotic stars is primarily a combination of free-free emission of the ionization region and optically thick blackbody emission of the cooler dust components of the system. When combined with contemporaneous multi-wavelength observations, millimeter-wave observations can be used to test binary models of symbiotic stars and provide insight on the geometry and physical properties of these systems.

item.title: Cataclysmic variables from Gaia XP spectra: The Gaia emission-line magnitude (GEM) diagram
item.description: arXiv:2607.28736v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Gaia DR3 opens a new window for the census of Galactic stellar populations in all-sky surveys, specifically for identifying cataclysmic variables (CVs). While the majority of CVs are distributed below the main sequence on the Gaia HR diagram, identifying them among dominant background stellar populations remains a significant challenge. Here, we present the Gaia Emission-line Magnitude (GEM) diagram - a tool designed to isolate CV candidates from background stars located below the main sequence. Using Gaia photometric data and low-resolution BP/RP (XP) spectra, we construct the GEM diagram by plotting the extinction-corrected absolute magnitude ($M_{G0}$) against the pseudo-equivalent width of the H$\alpha$ line ($pgEW_{H\alpha}$), which is computed via a Gaussian line-profile approximation. We find that known CVs and major stellar background populations, including white dwarfs, hot subdwarfs, and white dwarf-main sequence binaries, occupy distinct regions on the GEM diagram, reflecting both their physical properties and the low-resolution nature of the Gaia XP spectra. We define an empirical selection line on the GEM diagram to separate true H$\alpha$-emitting CVs from background contaminants. As a proof of concept, we apply the GEM diagram to a Gaia volume-limited sample within 250 pc ($G<17.5$ mag) distributed below the main sequence, recovering known CVs. Additionally, we identify three new CV candidates whose accreting nature is supported by archival X-ray data and optical variability. Compared to traditional optical color-based selection techniques, the GEM diagram uses Gaia's low-resolution spectra for initial target identification in all-sky surveys. This provides a more reliable framework for the statistical selection of CV candidates prior to ground-based spectroscopic follow-up and can be scaled to future Gaia data releases to map Galactic emission-line star populations.

item.title: No Significant Rotation of the Spiral Structure in the IM Lup Protoplanetary Disk
item.description: arXiv:2611.07405v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spiral structures are often observed in protoplanetary disks, but their origins remain uncertain. Yoshida et al. (2025) reported a pattern speed consistent with local Keplerian rotation for the $m=2$ spiral in the dusty disk around IM Lup using multi-epoch ALMA observations, supporting a gravitational instability (GI)-driven origin. However, recent studies revise the disk geometry of IM Lup, motivating a reassessment of its spiral pattern speed. In this study, we reanalyze the disk geometry of the same multi-epoch data using visibility-based continuum emission modeling. The inferred disk geometries differ from those adopted in previous studies by a few degrees but are consistent across epochs and with recent independent estimates based on gas emission analyses. The revised geometries yield weaker residuals and more physically plausible radial spiral phase profiles. Unlike previous studies, our remeasured spiral pattern speeds are consistent with zero rotation within the uncertainties. We conclude that the previously reported Keplerian-like motion can be explained by a mismatch in the adopted disk geometry, which affects the spiral phases measured in Band 6 (2017, 2019) and Band 7 (2024) differently. In addition, we identify a tentative large-scale one-armed spiral-like structure extending beyond the known $m=2$ spiral, which may provide clues to additional perturbations, such as an embedded planet or late-stage infall. Future high-resolution Band 6 observations with a longer time baseline will be essential for more accurately determining the spiral pattern speed.
item.dc:creator: Yuto Hiraide, Masataka Aizawa, Munetake Momose

item.title: Anisotropic Coulomb Interaction in Strongly Magnetized Electron Gas at Zero Temperature in Relativistic Quantum Framework
item.description: arXiv:2611.25688v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a microscopic derivation of Debye screening in a Landau-quantized electron gas subject to a strong magnetic field. By calculating the photon self-energy within the RPA framework, we explore how Landau levels influence the screening properties of the electron gas. Due to the quantum periodicity of Landau levels, the screening behavior is relatively insensitive to variations in the carrier density within each occupation cycle compared to the drastic changes induced by the magnetic field strength. Within a single occupation cycle, the Kohn anomaly dominates the low-density regime; at higher densities, its characteristic momentum shifts into the asymptotic high-momentum regime, rendering its singular contribution less prominent over the active screening domain and allowinga smooth orientation-dependent anisotropy to govern the system. Furthermore, a subtle competition in directional screening is observed between the parallel and perpendicular directions to the field depending on the density domain. At lower field strengths, multiple quantum oscillations emerge from the simultaneous participation of various Landau levels, marking a qualitative transition toward the isotropic three-dimensional limit. Our findings reveal anisotropic screening effects and provide insights into the behavior of charged impurities in such systems.
